facts.text: Venice, originally called the “Venice of America,” was founded by Abbot Kinney in 1905 as a beach resort town.
The name “Venice of America” reflects Kinney’s vision to model the city after Venice, Italy, with canals and Italian‑style architecture.
Venice is the birthplace of modern progressive skateboarding, celebrated in the documentary *Dogtown and Z‑Boys* and the film *The Lords of Dogtown*.
The Venice Beach boardwalk is famous for its murals, including Rip Cronk’s 1990 piece *Venice Beach* and the 2012 work *Touch of Venice* by Jonas.
The legendary rock band The Doors formed in Venice in 1965, with members Ray Manzarek and Jim Morrison hailing from the area.
Venice Beach will host the triathlon, marathon start, and road cycling events during the 2028 Summer Olympics.
